members.name: gap_relative_index_v1
members.thesis: When a stock gaps significantly more than its parent index (e.g., RELIANCE gaps -1.5% but NIFTY only gaps -0.3%), the excess gap (stock gap minus index gap) tends to mean-revert within the session. The excess gap represents stock-specific over-reaction layered on top of the market move. By isolating
entry_long: excess_gap < -0.5 (stock gapped down more than beta-adjusted index)
entry_short: excess_gap > 0.5 (stock gapped up more than beta-adjusted index)
members.exit_stop: excess_gap extends by 40% from open OR relative_return loss > 0.4%
filters: NIFTY not in extreme trend (> 2% move) to maintain beta stability
weaknesses: Beta estimation from 60-day daily data may not reflect the true intraday beta, especially during volatile sessions when correlations break down
The 'no stock-specific news' filter is subjective and difficult to automate — some information leaks through chat groups and social media before formal announcements
If the excess gap is caused by a large institutional block deal (which may not be publicly known), the position can be in the wrong direction for extended periods
members.prior_art: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) decomposition of returns into systematic and idiosyncratic. Daniel & Moskowitz (2016) on momentum crashes. Gap-specific adaptation is novel.

members.name: index_gap_constituent_lag_v1
members.thesis: When Nifty50 gaps significantly (> 0.5%), some constituents gap less than their beta would suggest — these 'laggards' tend to catch up in the first 30 minutes as ETF creation/redemption and index arbitrage forces push them toward fair value.
